headline: Bounce into $629-651 supply — short the rejection

factors.evidence: ~2.5-month range $583–690. A blow-off failed breakout to $746 reversed hard, then the crash swept the $583 floor to $556 and reclaimed it. Failed at both extremes — still a range, no established trend.
Price $606 is below the 20 EMA; the 20 has rolled under the 50 (bearish compression).
Price well below the decline's AVWAP (and below the full-window AVWAP $640).
Below the midline and below its signal MA (48.0) — momentum regime is bearish.
The crash printed enormous volume (226K → 346K → 232K); the bounce is on light volume (77K–79K). Textbook distribution.

Clean LH/LL off $746 down to $556. Off the low, price is now making higher lows ($556→$559→$570→$585) and higher highs ($579→$598→$610) and reclaimed the 20 EMA — but the larger 4H lower-high (~$650+) is not yet broken.
Price well below the decline's AVWAP; not reclaimed.
Recovered from oversold and is now well above its signal MA (36.9) and back over the midline — a sharp momentum turn (bullish divergence off the $556 low).
A 65K spike marked the $556 low (exhaustion); the bounce/base is on lighter volume — not yet demand expansion.

setup.type: Rejection Short at $629–651 supply (trend-aligned) — not yet triggered
setup.thesis: Wait and short the rejection at $629–651 — where the bearish bias, the location (selling into the daily EMA + AVWAP + 0.5-fib wall), and the R:R (~3.5–5:1) all line up. It triggers on a 4H rejection / failure to reclaim $650. Secondary: breakdown short on a 4H close below $556.
setup.not: It is not the bounce long — that is a tactical scalp at best (long $583–590, hard stop <$556, take profit into $629–636 and flip), explicitly the scrape and not a swing.

analyst_summary: BNB is bearish-transitional and price sits in no-man's-land ($606) between the $556 sweep low and the dense $629–651 supply wall (daily 20/50 EMA + daily & 4H decline AVWAP + 0.5 fib).

Scored symmetrically, the trend-aligned Rejection Short into $629–651 is the highest-quality thesis (bias-aligned, sells into confluence supply with $50–90 of air below, ~3.5–5:1 R:R) — but it is not yet triggered; it sets up on a 4H rejection / failure to reclaim $650.

The bounce long is the only thing actionable right now and it is the weakest of the three options — against the bearish bias, poorly located under supply, ~1:1 R:R — so it rates a tactical scalp ($583–590, stop <$556, flip into $629–636), not a swing.

Method note: this is the de-biased re-run. The original BNB output led with the bounce long and buried the short in the failure box; forcing all three trades (bounce-long / rejection-short / breakdown-short) onto identical axes put the trend-aligned short first and the long last — same data, opposite headline. The default-killer was scoring location (buying under supply is penalized) and separating 'live now' from 'best setup', not simply adding a short thesis.
bottom_line: The trend-aligned short into $629–651 is the highest-quality thesis but is not yet triggered; the bounce long is a tactical scalp only. Wait to short the rejection (or a 4H close <$556), don't chase the bounce as a swing.
